Evidence is empty. No external market support, company forecast or detailed causal decomposition supports precise target driver choices. Historical references support transparent analyst assumptions only.

Contract bounds are guardrails, not forecast estimates. Bear profitability generally requires higher underlying ratios, catastrophe losses and tax rates, and lower favorable development and income; bull reverses those directions. Premium growth and share-count choices require explicit judgment.

The nonnegative favorable-development bound excludes adverse reserve development, and the underlying-ratio ceiling of 1.0 limits stress severity. These are scenario coverage constraints, not evidence that worse outcomes cannot occur.
No supported target realized-gain assumption is supplied. Core EPS can be modeled under the contract; GAAP net income or GAAP EPS requires a separately disclosed reconciliation assumption.
